title: The Long Valley Bix festival and the kitchen reunion
summary: Virginia describes going to Bill Donahoe's Long Valley Bix festival with the Rykers and walking into the kitchen to find Chauncey, Bill Rank, Doc Ryker and Bill Challis after 50 years.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Did you go into the Bix Beiderbecke festivals at Davenport?
No, we went up to Long Valley. This Bill Donahoe...
Did you really? So did I.
We went there first
You weren't there when I was there. Believe me, I would have seen you.
For several years we went there. Until last year....
They didn't have one.

When we first came up from Florida, I had kept a correspondence with Doc and Norma for many years, all our life, practically. And they were en route to Bill Donahoe's for this big festival. And Norma had told me...
You went the year before I did. I don't remember the year now though.

Norma phoned me and said they were going to this thing. They would like to stop off and visit with me, especially since my sister was here visiting also, flew in from California. So they stopped off here and

stayed a couple of nights. And they said, why don't you girls come up to that festival. I wonder if it's possible for you. Do you mind if we call Bill Donahoe. And she did and she said, two of Charlie Horvath's two sisters are here and this is where we're staying. And they would like to attend the festival if you wouldn't mind. And they said, by all means bring them. So we went up to this Bix festival, which was in Long Valley. And of course it was a very enthralling and entrancing meeting. Because you know how their home is with lovely antique, old home.
Yes, right.
Remember the kitchen there?
Sure do.

The random width floors and all the antiques. And I remember I walked into the kitchen and there were several men standing around there with their cocktails. After 50 years, it's a little hard to recognize people. So I just walked into the kitchen and said, anybody here who played with the Jean Goldkette orchestra in Detroit in the twenties. And they turned around like a group. Well, I'm Charlie Horvath's sister. And everybody practically fainted.
I'll bet. And one of them standing there was Chauncey. Standing in the kitchen after 50 years.
After 50 years.
50 years, incredible.
Bill Rank and...
Was Bill Rank there too?
Yes, Bill Rank was there.
And Doc Ryker.
And Doc Ryker.
He saw them all.
Joe Venuti, no Joe Venuti, he was not there. He wasn't there.
But you walked in the kitchen and there was Bill Rank and Doc Ryker and Chauncey Morehouse, all standing around. Yeah.
And Bill Challis.
Bill Charles.
Bill Charles was there. Well I'm telling you our mouths were just went.
I'll bet. Did they work with you?
They certainly did. I was 16. I'm a senior citizen now.
That's great.
